title: Parameter spec authoring lints and runtime repair playbook
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Create a practical, prescriptive playbook for authoring JSON parameter schemas for function/tool calls and a layered validation system (author-time lints, SDK-level checks, runtime validation and repair). The deliverable is a concise guideline + lint rules + runtime repair heuristics that reduce customer errors and make error messages actionable. Goals: 1) reduce invalid-calls customer incidents by 60% for first-party tool contracts, 2) provide deterministic downgrade/fallback behavior when schemas change, 3) standardize developer-facing error messages across SDKs and console.
acceptance_criteria: Authoring guide published in /docs/call-schemas with examples for common patterns (enums, deeply nested objects, optional arrays)
Set of 12 lint rules implemented in schema-linter with autofix where safe
SDK checks integrated to surface lint warnings during local development (Node + Python) and documented
Runtime validation library updated to return structured diagnostics and suggested repair actions
A fallback policy documented and implemented: (strict->coerce->fallback-model->error) with telemetry hooks
Regression tests covering coercion, rejection, and streaming partial outputs for 8 representative tool contracts
technical_notes: We propose a three-layer validation approach: (1) Author-time lints + template samples, (2) SDK preflight checks + local example runner, (3) Runtime validator with repair transformers and explicit error codes.
Lint rules should be conservative: prefer warning over error for non-breaking patterns. Example autofix: convert single-value enum union to explicit enum array when safe.

Runtime repair heuristics: trim unknown object keys if allowUnknown=false becomes false due to version drift, coerce primitive strings to numbers when safe, normalize date formats to ISO-8601. All repairs must attach a RepairHint to telemetry.

Compatibility layer: maintain a 'compat profile' per client version that maps deprecated field names to current names and allows fuzzy coercion thresholds. Profiles stored as versioned manifests in S3 and hot-reloaded.

Streaming contracts: when streaming structured outputs, validate each chunk independently and surface partial diagnostics; do not abort the stream unless a terminal schema violation occurs. Provide 'partial_validation' metadata in stream frames.
Error codes: follow the pattern RFN_[L|S|R]_[nnn] where L=lint, S=sdk, R=runtime. Example: RFN_R_003 -> 'Coerced string->number', RFN_L_010 -> 'Enum recommended to be explicit array'.
decision_log: 2025-02-18: Chose to implement linter as a standalone npm/pyproject package (schema-linter) rather than bundling inside SDKs. Rationale: reuse across web UI, CLI, CI checks. (Decision by Lucas, Ayesha, Mei)
2025-02-26: Agreed on three-tier validation stack and the repair-first policy with explicit telemetry. Opted against silent best-effort conversions for nested objects (too risky).
2025-03-04: Streaming partial-validation model approved: validate per-frame and add 'validation_frame' with warnings; only send terminal rejection on unrecoverable token-level mismatch.
comments: Ayesha (2025-02-13): Initial draft of lint rules attached. Need feedback on which rules should autofix vs warn.
Mei Chen (Design) (2025-02-15): UX note: error messages must include sample corrected payload where possible to reduce friction in Console and SDK error overlays.
Jordan Lee (SDK) (2025-02-20): Node SDK can surface linter warnings at build time; Python SDK wants a runtime import hook. We should standardize the linter API first.
Lucas (2025-03-01): Implemented prototype for string->number coercion with telemetry. See PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1234
SRE (2025-03-05): Telemetry schema change required to include repair_hint and compat_profile_id. Added as dependency.
QA (2025-03-10): Found edge case: when arrays are interleaved with streaming frames, repair logic sometimes reorders elements. Added test and marked as blocker for stable-release.
Product (2025-03-12): Prioritize the linter + SDK preflight for GA; runtime repair heuristics can be behind a feature flag initially.
Lucas (2025-03-18): Updated docs with examples for legacy compatibility mappings. Preparing release branch for schema-linter@v0.3.0
